transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’m worn out all the time. Even if I spend a full night in bed, I wake up feeling like my body is made of sandbags. Getting through a workday—or even doing something like folding laundry—takes everything I have.
Has anyone told you that you snore loudly or seem to stop breathing at times while you're asleep?
No one’s mentioned that to me. I’m not really sure what happens while I’m asleep.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you noticed feeling down, depressed, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Yeah. Most mornings I wake up with this heavy, flat feeling in my chest. I’ll sit at the kitchen table just staring out at the yard, and it feels like there isn’t really a good version of the future coming.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks of low mood and fatigue—prior to this current episode?
I’m not sure. I can’t really think of another time that was like this for weeks.
Have you noticed any unexplained weight gain or increased sensitivity to cold recently?
No, I haven’t noticed any weight gain, and I don’t think I’ve been more sensitive to cold than usual.
After you physically or mentally exert yourself—even something mild like folding laundry—do you notice that your exhaustion gets significantly worse for the next day or two?

Yes. Even small things can wipe me out. I’ll do something like fold laundry, and it feels like it takes everything I have—then I’m even more exhausted afterward, sometimes into the next day. Even after a full night in bed, I still feel worn out, like my body’s made of sandbags.
How long have you been experiencing this constant, unrefreshing fatigue and post-exertional exhaustion—days, weeks, or months?
About two months, I think—since we took on the mortgage. Things swung from that really overcharged push into this low stretch, and the exhaustion’s been there through it.
You mentioned an 'overcharged push' before this low stretch began—during that time, did you notice needing much less sleep than usual while still feeling full of energy?
I'm not sure. I remember having a lot more drive during that time, but I didn't really keep track of how much I was sleeping.
During that period when you felt full of drive and energy, about how many days in a row did that heightened state last?
It was around the time we took on the mortgage, about two months ago. Then it shifted from that really overcharged business push into this low stretch.
During that high-energy period before your mood dropped, did you notice yourself talking much faster than usual or feeling like your thoughts were racing?
I’m not really sure. I know I was very driven, but I can’t say whether I was talking faster or whether my thoughts were racing.

During that high-energy period when you took on the mortgage, did you find yourself making bigger or riskier decisions than you normally would, like spending more money or taking on new commitments impulsively?
I’m not sure. The mortgage was a big commitment, obviously, but I can’t really say whether I was being unusually impulsive or making other risky decisions then.
Have you noticed any dizziness, lightheadedness, or shortness of breath, especially with mild exertion, over the past couple of months?
I haven’t really noticed anything like that.
Have you noticed your skin or nails looking unusually pale, or have you had any unusual cravings, like wanting to chew on ice?
No, I haven’t noticed my skin or nails looking pale, and I don’t have cravings like chewing ice.
During that high-energy period around the mortgage, did you find yourself sleeping much less than usual—say only a few hours a night—yet still not feeling tired the next day?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember my sleep being that different, or feeling like I could get by on only a few hours.
During that high-energy period around the mortgage, did you feel unusually elated, euphoric, or 'on top of the world'—more than just being driven or busy?
Yeah, I think so. For the first few weeks after we signed the mortgage papers, I felt almost lit up and unstoppable at times. But then I’d snap at my husband or coworkers over really tiny delays.
During that lit-up, unstoppable stretch after signing the mortgage, about how many days in a row did that elevated feeling last?
It wasn’t just a couple of days. Since we took on the mortgage about two months ago, my mood has kind of swung from that overcharged push into this low stretch.
During that few weeks when you felt lit up and unstoppable after the mortgage, did your husband or coworkers comment that you seemed noticeably different from your usual self?
My husband’s noticed more lately that I move around the house like I’m underwater. And if he asks me something simple, it can take me a while to answer because the words come out really slowly.
Over these past two months, have you noticed a persistent sore throat, tender or swollen lymph nodes in your neck, or new muscle and joint aches without any swelling or redness?
No, I haven’t noticed any of those things.

During that lit-up, unstoppable stretch after the mortgage, did you feel unusually confident or capable—like you could handle things better than anyone else, or that you were somehow more special or important than usual?

Yeah. For a while I was convinced I could outgrow my firm quickly and start my own consulting business—do it better than anybody around me. I hadn’t actually lined up clients or anything, but at the time it felt like I could just make it happen.

Thinking back to that lit-up, unstoppable stretch after the mortgage, can you tell me roughly how many days in a row you felt that way before it started to shift—was it more like 4 days, a week, or longer?
It was after we took on the mortgage, about two months ago. I had that really overcharged push at first, and then it shifted into this low stretch I’ve been in.
